- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weakly positive or negative (e.g., <0.4 or <0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted in the short-term forecast (e.g., 30d) — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overcorrect downward — forecast dips too early or too far.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds too much upward bias in high-sentiment periods.
- Forecast horizon-specific error: 30d forecasts are consistently too high in early 2025, especially when sentiment is rising — model overweights momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model smooths too much — misses sudden reversals or breakout events.
